# Decisions and assumptions

spec

These choices were made where the specification left room. Each can be changed.

The reachability check (DOC203) is skipped when none of the roots exists, because every document would then be an orphan; DOC205 already reports the missing roots.

Custom rules keep their own level when the recommended preset is switched off, because they exist only when the project defines them.

The single files `docs/out.md` and `docs/out.html` take their names from the output folder (`out` and `outFull` plus an extension), so no settings exist for them. They are not checked by `docc check` and are meant to stay out of git.

The single HTML file is built from the same Markdown as the single Markdown file, converted by the library goldmark with the GitHub extensions, and cut into blocks at markers that docc puts before every element; the marker name is chosen so that no text of the page contains it. Page anchors are the document id and field anchors are the document id, two hyphens and the field anchor.

Every document has a kind schema (DOC109 is core) and the check is flat: a document is checked by the schema of its own kind only, schemas do not inherit from each other.

A strict kind is closed by docc, not by `unevaluatedProperties`: the schema states a boolean `additionalProperties`, and docc collects the allowed names from the top-level properties, `allOf` branches and local `$ref` targets. This way an unknown field gets one clear message with a suggested name, instead of a validator error about a keyword the author did not write.

`docc build` confirms the links that are not yet in `docc.lock` on its own. A separate confirmation of every added link would be a ritual that people run without reading; the lock only has to notice when a target changes after a link exists.

Code gets a hash only inside `docc:begin` and `docc:end` regions. A hash of a whole file would warn on every unrelated edit, and warnings nobody acts on teach people to ignore them.

Numbers of pages and sections are computed from the tree when `numbering` is on, so they never go out of date. Only a number typed at the start of a title or a section key is reported (DOC314); the text of fields is not checked, because a number there is part of the content.

A link exists only as a reference in the text. A separate list of links would repeat the text and drift from it, and a reference in a sentence also says why the documents are related.

docc is a public open source project (MIT) with releases on GitHub, installers, `docc update` and the skill installed by `npx skills add`. The first users are the author's team; there are no sales, plans or support promises.

`docc ack` confirms only links that changed and prints each one, because a command that silently confirms every link on a document lets an agent clear warnings about sources nobody read. `docc init` writes `maxWarnings` 0 so that a stale link (DOC209) stops `docc check`, the pre-commit hook and CI; a warning that blocks nothing is ignored.

DOC209 is one diagnostic per source document and target document, at the first link, so a document that links to two or more parts of one target is not warned more than once. A link to an anchor or a field is warned about only when that part changes, which is why the hint advises it.

DOC110 warns about a free field spelled almost like a reserved key (`parnet`, `hiden`) that the kind schema does not declare. The reserved fields are the only ones with a meaning, so a typo would otherwise be silent prose.

`docc build` deletes from the output folder only what it generated (pages with the GENERATED mark, copies of images that exist in the sources, file manager junk). With any other file there it refuses and lists the files, because a silent deletion loses work. A marker file and `--dry-run` were not added.

A launch or config error in JSON is the usual report with a diagnostic of code `config`, `usage` or `error`, and every error of `docc.json` is listed at once, so an agent parses one shape and fixes the file in one pass. Diagnostics stay ordered errors first, then by file and position: moving warnings in among errors was not done.

The history of a block comes from Git, not from a journal of docc: it covers the whole past of a project at once and adds no file. A block is one element of the JSON (a paragraph of an array, a field value), not one line of text: the elements keep their pointers when a list item is inserted inside a paragraph. Only committed states and the working tree are seen; a renamed field or section starts its history again.

The HTML application uses Preact with htm in one embedded file instead of a framework with a build step, so `go build` stays the only build and the project needs no Node.

Comments are kept in the browser and leave it as a file, because the HTML file has no server. `docc.comments.json` stores them one per line with the status `open` or `done`, so a change of status is a one-line diff. docc does not change the text by a comment: an agent reads `docc comments`, agrees the change with a person and marks the comment.

Dictation uses the speech recognition of the browser: Chrome and Edge send the sound to their speech service. A Chromium without the keys of that service and Firefox show no microphone button; the comment is typed.

The rules are listed in [Rules and diagnostics](rules.md) and the settings in [Configuration](config.md).

## Not verified

Windows and macOS were not run: only Linux was available. The two GitHub workflows (tests and releases) run on Linux only, so the Windows and macOS builds are cross-compiled and untested.

The criterion that an agent fixes 9 of 10 synthetic errors in two iterations was not measured.
